Class ChildContext

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.inject.context.ChildContext
All Implemented Interfaces:
Context
public final class ChildContext extends Object implements Context
A child Context: nearest-ancestor local bindings first (walking up through any intermediate ChildContexts), then the parent. Unscoped parent beans are rebuilt at this — the deepest — context so their dependencies see the full child binding stack. A bean of a child-local scope (one with no Scope service) is built once by the nearest context of the chain that hosts its scope, this one included, which caches it; its dependencies resolve through that host. Other scoped beans and everything without a BeanDefinition anchor to the parent unchanged.

    • ChildContext

      public ChildContext(Context parent, Map<Key<?>, Provider<?>> bindings, Class<? extends Annotation> scope)
      Creates a child context over parent that hosts the child-local scope: it builds and caches the instances of that scope's beans resolved through it or its descendants.
      Parameters:
      parent - the parent context resolutions fall back to
      bindings - the child's own bindings, by key
      scope - the child-local scope this context hosts
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if scope is handled by a Scope service, or if the root of the chain is not a DefaultContext
      IllegalStateException - if parent is closed
      ScopeResolutionException - if a bean of scope depends directly on a bean of another child-local scope that no context of the chain hosts; the message lists every such dependency
      UnsatisfiedDependencyException - if a bean of scope depends on a key that neither the root, nor this context, nor one of its parents binds; the message lists every such dependency

    • createScoped

      public <T> T createScoped(ScopedProduct product, @Nullable Consumer<? super T> preDestroy, Function<? super Context, ? extends T> instance)
      Description copied from interface: Context
      Creates the instance of a child-local assisted product, and caches it in the nearest context of the chain that hosts its scope, by its key. Generated assisted factories call this for a recipe with a child-local scope.

      The default rejects every call, so minimal Context implementations need not host scopes.

      Specified by:
      createScoped in interface Context
      Type Parameters:
      T - the product type
      Parameters:
      product - the product to create
      preDestroy - the product's @PreDestroy callback, run when its host closes, or null
      instance - builds the instance through the context it is given: the host's, so the product's dependencies resolve where it is cached
      Returns:
      the created instance

    • close

      public void close()
      Closes this child context: rejects further resolution through it, including through the providers it returned, closes its live child contexts, newest first, then destroys the instances of its hosted scope (invoking each factory's @PreDestroy) in reverse creation order. Failures are collected as suppressed exceptions on the first one thrown, so every child and every instance is still given a chance to close or destroy. Never closes the parent. Idempotent.
      Specified by:
      close in interface Context
